CCA class 13 - minimum number of years

Leasehold improvements are written off over the lease term plus the first renewal period, but never faster than over this number of years (the allowance is at most one fifth of the capital cost). Income Tax Regulations, Schedule III. Source: https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/C.R.C.,_c._945/
CCA class 13 - maximum number of years

The lease term plus the first renewal period counted for class 13 is capped at this number of years. Income Tax Regulations, Schedule III. Source: https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/C.R.C.,_c._945/
CCA class 12 - half-year rule exemption threshold

Small tools, kitchen utensils and medical or dental instruments of class 12 costing less than this amount are not subject to the half-year rule and are fully deductible in the year of acquisition. Income Tax Regulations, Schedule II, class 12 paragraphs (b), (c), (e) and (v), and section 1100(2). Source: https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/sole-proprietorships-partnerships/report-business-income-expenses/claiming-capital-cost-allowance/classes-depreciable-property.html

Enhanced first-year allowance of accelerated (AIIP, acquired after 2018-11-20 and before 2025, available for use before 2028) and reaccelerated (RIIP, acquired after 2024, available for use before 2034) investment incentive property, by acquisition and available-for-use date. A class parameter l10n_ca.cca.class_<number>.aiip.windows replaces these windows for its class (classes 44, 46 and 50). 'hyr' multiplies the normal first-year allowance of a class subject to the half-year rule (3 = 1.5 x rate x cost), 'no_hyr' that of a class that is not. Property that was depreciated before by another person and was previously owned by the taxpayer or a non-arm's length person, or acquired on a rollover, does not qualify. Income Tax Regulations sections 1100(2), 1104(4) and 1104(4.01). The reaccelerated investment incentive (RIIP, property acquired after 2024 and available for use before 2034) and the extended immediate expensing were enacted by Bill C-15, Budget 2025 Implementation Act, No. 1 (S.C. 2026, c. 3, Royal Assent 2026-03-26); the reaccelerated incentive applies to property acquired after 2024. Sources: https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/sole-proprietorships-partnerships/report-business-income-expenses/claiming-capital-cost-allowance/accelerated-investment-incentive.html ; https://www.budget.canada.ca/update-miseajour/2024/report-rapport/tm-mf-en.html ; https://www.parl.ca/documentviewer/en/45-1/bill/C-15/royal-assent

First-year write-off rate of new additions of class 44 (patents) that are AIIP or RIIP acquired and available for use after 2024-04-15 and before 2027 (productivity-enhancing assets, Budget 2024; Quebec harmonized in Information Bulletin 2024-6). Property that becomes available for use after 2026 is not expensed: its first-year allowance comes from the class parameter aiip.windows. Income Tax Regulations section 1100(2), element A paragraphs (c.1) to (c.3) and element A.1 paragraphs (c) to (e): the factor added to 1 and multiplied by the class rate gives 100%. Enhanced first-year allowance of class 44 (patents) property that is not expensed, replacing l10n_ca.cca.aiip.windows for this class; same keys. Class 44 is excluded from the general factor 1/2 of reaccelerated property: its factor is nil once the immediate expensing window closes, so property acquired after 2024 and available for use in 2027 to 2033 enters the CCA base at its full cost without the half-year rule (2 times the normal first-year allowance), not 1.5 times. Accelerated property acquired before 2025 keeps the general windows. Income Tax Regulations section 1100(2), element A paragraphs (a) and (c.1) to (c.3), element A.1 paragraphs (a) and (c) to (e), and element C (the half-year rule does not apply to accelerated or reaccelerated property); section 1104(4) and (4.01). Enacted by Bill C-15, Budget 2025 Implementation Act, No. 1 (S.C. 2026, c. 3, Royal Assent 2026-03-26). Source: consolidated Income Tax Regulations, https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/C.R.C.,_c._945/FullText.html
